errors.english: When butter is poured from the ladle, the flames should take the shapes of
errors.why: The verse lists 'the shape of the ladle used for the butter offering' as one of the auspicious flame shapes, not a circumstance of pouring.

note: A faithful rendering of the fire-sign verses and the remedial procedure; one item of the shape list is turned into a temporal clause.

errors.english: It is explained: Mundane beings arise through their own essence
errors.why: The verses that follow are quotations of the rejected svabhāva, Īśvara and puruṣa causal theories, but the English introduces them as if they were the commentator's own explanation.

note: Generally accurate; the quoted opponents' views (nature, the Lord, the Person) need to be marked as the views being rejected.

errors.why: The phrase is a lemma from the root text, 'the rest is indeterminate'; 'they say' (ཞེས་ཟེར་རོ) belongs to the end of the preceding sentence, so nothing here is attributed to other teachers.

note: Sound overall, but a root-text lemma is presented as the opinion of 'others', which misattributes the passage on neutral mind.

errors.why: ཡང་དག་བདེན་པ renders the Chinese name of Paramārtha (Zhendi), whose commentary this author cites; 'Satyavadin, True Speaker' is an invented name, and it recurs later as 'Master Satyavadin's commentary'.

errors.english: by (Lang) [note: Likely referring to a specific translator or regional recension]
errors.why: ལང་གི་ཚེ་བསྒྱུར་བ means the translation made in the Liang period (Paramārtha's Chinese version of the Mahāyānasaṃgraha commentary), not a translator named Lang.

fix.find: by (Lang) [note: Likely referring to a specific translator or regional recension]
fix.replace: translated in the Liang period [note: Paramārtha's Chinese translation under the Liang dynasty]

note: The argument is followed correctly, but the Chinese-source references (Paramārtha, the Liang translation) are misidentified throughout.
A faithful translation of the ten benefits of the dharma-eye and the nine knowledges.

errors.english: it is well said that the (Madhyamaka) Middle Way and (Yogacara) Yoga Practice school share the same philosophical conclusion
errors.why: The Tibetan is conditional: it would be good IF Mādhyamikas and Yogācāras had the same tenet on this point; the English asserts that they do.

errors.english: it is without the subtle and complete syllable (Hum), without vowels, without the moon, and without the (bindu) the drop or point of energy
errors.why: The passage lists grades of the subtle mudrā (the complete subtle HŪṂ with vowel, moon and bindu; the form without them; the mustard-seed bindu; etc.), and does not say that HŪṂ is absent.

errors.english: one line of text regarding the conventional understanding of generation stage
errors.why: This is leaked editorial text; the Tibetan sentence (continued on the next side with མ་ཡིན་གྱི) says the term is NOT used here in the worldly sense.

fix.find: is used here because it is well known to worldly people one line of text regarding the conventional understanding of generation stage.
fix.replace: is used here not in the sense known to worldly people, but...

note: The tantric doctrine is mostly followed, but there is a conditional rendered as an assertion, a muddled list of subtle forms, and leaked junk text at the end.

errors.why: ཐ་སྙད means conventional designation (vyavahāra); 'ultimate' is the opposite.
མངོན་པའི་ང་རྒྱལ is abhimāna, the conceit of having attained what one has not, not ordinary pride, and it applies to 'others' as well as to ordinary beings.

note: Follows the sūtra lemmata closely; one technical reversal (conventional rendered as ultimate).

errors.english: (mukaka) likely a species of wood apple or similar medicinal plant
errors.why: This is the Āyurvedic muṣkakādi group (muṣkaka, Schrebera), not wood apple.

errors.english: the substance called (sarala) pine resin, (ko-nyon-tse) an unidentified herbal ingredient
errors.why: The Tibetan names one ingredient, 'what is called sarala, i.e. ko-nyon-tse', but the English splits it into two items.

note: The medical procedure and the dosages are rendered correctly; there are some doubtful plant identifications in glosses.

errors.english: the (Siddhartha) white mustard and (Khadira) acacia catechu are consecrated
errors.why: The Tibetan refers to the ritual pegs made of [gold] (continuing གསེར་ from the previous side) and of khadira wood; there is no white mustard here.

fix.find: the (Siddhartha) white mustard and (Khadira) acacia catechu are consecrated
fix.replace: the [pegs] made of [gold] and of (Khadira) acacia catechu are consecrated

note: The four quarters of the twenty-eight wrathful deities, and their colours, are all correctly rendered; only the opening misidentifies the consecrated pegs.
A faithful translation of the cosmological description of the golden mountain ranges.
